title: Tell a deoptimisation from a tier change in a compile log

blocks.text: The search service's latency jumps for a few seconds several times a day, and the team now runs it with `-XX:+PrintCompilation`. Each jump comes with a burst of `made not entrant` lines, and nobody can tell by eye which of them matter. The on-call engineer wants a small tool that, for one method, answers two questions from the log alone.

`CompileLog` already reads the log: it skips every line that isn't a compile line and turns the rest into `Line` records, in log order. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/CompileLog.java`:

items: `currentTier(method)`: the tier of the code that a call to the method made now would enter, or `0` for the interpreter;

`deoptimizations(method)`: how many times the JIT threw away the method's code because it could no longer be used. The method's ordinary progress through the tiers is not an incident and doesn't count.

blocks.text: Both answers are about the code that calls enter. About fifteen lines in total.
The tests feed logs of other services' methods, with other ids and timestamps.

cases.says: a method compiled at tier 3 and then tier 4 runs at tier 4, a getter at tier 1, and a method with no compile line runs in the interpreter
tier-4 code made not entrant with no newer compile of the method counts as one deoptimisation
an OSR compile of the method's loop is not the code a new call enters
a tier-3 compile made not entrant after a tier-4 compile was installed leaves calls in the tier-4 code, not in the interpreter
after the tier-4 code is thrown away and the method is compiled again at tier 3, calls run at tier 3, not at the highest tier the method ever reached
a lower tier's code made not entrant because a newer compile replaced it is not a deoptimisation
code made not entrant before any newer compile existed is a deoptimisation, even if a higher tier is compiled later

origin.section: Compiled Code Rests on Assumptions, and a Class Loaded Later Can Make It Not Entrant

concepts: Code C2 compiled on the assumption that a class's method has one implementation is made not entrant when an overriding class loads, even if it is never called, and runs slower until C2 compiles it again.
A % line is an on-stack replacement compile of a loop, which a running call jumps into; it is not the code a new call enters.
A lower tier's code made not entrant after a newer compile of the same method was installed is a replacement: calls go to the newer code.

A method runs in the interpreter until its call and loop counters cross a threshold, then is compiled by C1 at tier 3 with profiling and by C2 at tier 4 from that profile; a trivial getter goes to tier 1.
